questions.q: A program that attaches itself to a file and spreads when the file is shared and run is a —
questions.solution: **Virus** = needs a host file and a run to spread.

questions.q: Malware that locks your files and demands money to release them is —
questions.solution: **Ransomware** holds data hostage — encrypt now, demand payment later (WannaCry, 2017).

questions.q: The correct set of Word alignment shortcuts is —
questions.solution: **LERJ**: Left, cEntre, Right, Justify.
questions.shortcut: LERJ — left to right across the line.

questions.q: Which statement about a firewall is TRUE?
options: It removes viruses from the hard disk
It replaces the need for backups
It filters the doorway but does not clean an infection inside
questions.solution: **Firewall filters traffic**; cleaning inside files is the antivirus's job.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A piece of cake
questions.solution: Cake = easy. *A piece of cake* = a task that needs almost no effort.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

If you **would have told** me earlier, I would have helped you.
questions.solution: The main clause *I would have helped* is a third conditional, so the *if*-clause must be past perfect: **If you had told me**. *would* never goes into the *if*-clause.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (2).
questions.solution: The clauses move in opposite directions — the walk demands nothing (+), yet few sustain it (−). Contrast is required: **yet**. *So/hence* would wrongly make continuation scarce a *result* of the walk's simplicity; *because* reverses the logic entirely.
questions.passage: Every morning, before the city fully (1) ______, a quiet crowd gathers in the parks. Retired teachers, young joggers and mothers returning from the dairy booths share the same paths. The morning walk costs nothing and demands no equipment, (2) ______ very few people manage to continue it beyond a fortnight. Doctors point out that its benefits depend almost entirely on (3) ______; twenty minutes on Sunday cannot undo six days of sitting. Over the weeks, a regular walker begins to (4) ______ noticeable changes — lighter steps, deeper sleep and a steadier mood. Perhaps that is why a group that walks together (5) ______ its own quiet discipline: the ones who arrive late feel they have missed something worth keeping.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

My grandmother is **a honest** and hardworking woman.
questions.solution: *Honest* begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent): **an honest**. 'The honest' over-specifics the generic sentence; 'a honestly' is wrong twice (article and part of speech).

questions.q: **National Youth Day** (12 January) marks the birth anniversary of:
questions.solution: **Swami Vivekananda** (born 12 January 1863); the date also opens the National Youth Festival.

questions.q: **Sindhi** was added to the Eighth Schedule by which amendment?
questions.solution: The **21st Amendment (1967)** added Sindhi. The 71st (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; the 92nd (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.

questions.q: President's Rule under **Article 356** can be continued, with parliamentary approvals, for a maximum of —
questions.solution: Six months at a time, extendable up to **three years** — beyond the first year it needs six-monthly approval plus the special conditions laid down by the 44th Amendment.

questions.q: **Dholavira**, noted for its water reservoirs and a 10-letter signboard, was excavated by —
questions.solution: **R.S. Bisht** excavated Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat) in the 1990s. S.R. Rao dug Lothal; B.B. Lal worked at Kalibangan; N.G. Majumdar at Chanhudaro.

questions.q: A tower subtends $75^\circ$ at a point $10$ m from its base (horizontal). Its height is:
questions.shortcut: $\tan75^\circ = 2+\sqrt3$ from the 45+30 identity. Keep it factored.

questions.q: The volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is: [Use $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution: $V=\pi r^2h=\frac{22}{7}\times49\times10=1540$ cu cm.

questions.q: The average of 7 consecutive multiples of 3 is 36. The largest of them is:
questions.solution: Middle (4th) = 36; largest = 5th... exact: $36 + 3 \times 3 = 45$? For 7 terms the largest is the middle + 3d $= 36 + 9 = 45$... wait, middle is the 4th of 7: offsets $-3d..+3d$, so largest $= 36 + 9 = 45$. The options' 42 corresponds to 5 consecutive; the consistent 7-term answer is 45.

questions.q: A sum of money invested at compound interest doubles itself in 8 years. In how many years will it become 8 times itself?
questions.solution: $8 = 2^3$: three doublings ⇒ $3 \times 8 = 24$ years.
questions.shortcut: Doubling chain at CI: 2× in 8 yrs ⇒ 4× in 16 ⇒ 8× in 24.

questions.q: **Facing East, a man takes two right turns and then one left turn. Which direction is he facing at the end?**
questions.solution: Net = +2 − 1 = +1 quarter turn. E + 1 clockwise step (E → S) = **South**.
questions.shortcut: Right-right-left = one right; E then one clockwise step = South.

questions.q: Three people — A, B and C — sit in a row facing north. **B sits in the middle. A sits to the immediate left of B.** Who sits at the **right end**?
questions.solution: Facing north, B's left is the west end. B = seat 2, A = seat 1, so C takes seat 3, the right end. Row (left to right): A B C.
questions.shortcut: Facing north: the person's left is your left on paper.

questions.q: Select the related letters: **DOT : TOD :: RAT : ?**
questions.solution: TOD is DOT **reversed**. Reversing RAT gives T-A-R → **TAR**.
questions.shortcut: Read the second cluster backwards; if it equals the first (or a constant shift of it), reverse the probe.
